Flight Delay Propagation Analysis¶

This notebook cleans flight data, engineers delay propagation features, performs exploratory data analysis, and produces statistical summaries to understand delay propagation.

1. Import Libraries¶

In [1]:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
sns.set_style('whitegrid')

3. Data Cleaning¶

  • Remove cancelled flights
  • Handle missing values
  • Create delay indicator

INSIGHTS and Reasoning¶

I decedided to remove a few columns that I felt would not be relevant to our desired analysis.
Things like Elapses time, air time, wheels on, taxi out, wheels off, taxi in, cancellation reason, would not be helpful in figuring out delay
I also removed late airplane delay as I will be creating a variable that I trust to be more accurate to describe the same thing

#replaces missing values of dep_delay with 0 assuming that they departed on time
df['DEPARTURE_DELAY'] = df['DEPARTURE_DELAY'].fillna(0)
#replaces missing values of arr_delay with 0 assuming that they arrived on time
df['ARRIVAL_DELAY'] = df['ARRIVAL_DELAY'].fillna(0)
#replaces missing values of air system delay with 0 assuming there was no delay from that
df['AIR_SYSTEM_DELAY'] = df['AIR_SYSTEM_DELAY'].fillna(0)
#replaces missing values of security delay with 0 assuming there was no delay from that
df['SECURITY_DELAY'] = df['SECURITY_DELAY'].fillna(0)
#replaces missing values of airline delay with 0 assuming there was no delay from that
df['AIRLINE_DELAY'] = df['AIRLINE_DELAY'].fillna(0)
#replaces missing values of weather delay with 0 assuming there was no delay from that
df['WEATHER_DELAY'] = df['WEATHER_DELAY'].fillna(0)
#dropping columns with missing arrival time as there isn't an easy assumption to make about that
df = df.dropna(subset=['ARRIVAL_TIME'])
#dropping columns with missing arrival time as there isn't an easy assumption to make about that
df = df.dropna(subset=['SCHEDULED_TIME'])
#Making sure there are no missing values
df.isna().sum().sort_values(ascending=False)

INSIGHTS¶

Replaced all missing delays with 0 as based on the data it could be assumed that there was no delay related to the specific delay category for those missing values
Also dropped rows where arrival time and scheudled time as there was no good way to impute values for those
Removed Cancelled column as after removing cancelled flights it no longer had a use

4. Feature Engineering¶

In [9]:
sort_cols = ['TAIL_NUMBER','FL_DATE','DEPARTURE_TIME']
#sorts the flights by aircraft, date of flight and departure time
df = df.sort_values(sort_cols)

#Adding column of the previous arrival time of the specific aircraft
df['prev_arr_time'] = df.groupby('TAIL_NUMBER')['ARRIVAL_TIME'].shift(1)

#adding column of the delay of arrival for previous flight
df['prev_arrival_delay'] = df.groupby('TAIL_NUMBER')['ARRIVAL_DELAY'].shift(1)

#making delay indicator column where if the flight was late more than 15min it is considered delayed
df['delay_indicator'] = (df['DEPARTURE_DELAY'] > 15).astype(int)

# convert times
df['DEPARTURE_TIME'] = df['DEPARTURE_TIME'].astype(str).str.zfill(4)
df['ARRIVAL_TIME'] = df['ARRIVAL_TIME'].astype(str).str.zfill(4)

for col in ['DEPARTURE_TIME', 'ARRIVAL_TIME']:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors='coerce')
    df[col] = df[col].apply(lambda x: f"{int(x):04d}" if pd.notna(x) else np.nan)

# create datetimes
df['dep_datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(
    df['FL_DATE'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d') + ' ' + df['DEPARTURE_TIME'],
    format='%Y-%m-%d %H%M',
    errors='coerce'
)

df['arr_datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(
    df['FL_DATE'].dt.strftime('%Y-%m-%d') + ' ' + df['ARRIVAL_TIME'],
    format='%Y-%m-%d %H%M',
    errors='coerce'
)

# fix overnight arrivals
df.loc[df['arr_datetime'] < df['dep_datetime'], 'arr_datetime'] += pd.Timedelta(days=1)

# sort properly
df = df.sort_values(['TAIL_NUMBER','dep_datetime'])

# previous flight info
df['prev_arr_datetime'] = df.groupby('TAIL_NUMBER')['arr_datetime'].shift(1)

#creating hour of day the aircraft departed column
df['hour'] = df['dep_datetime'].dt.hour

#creating congestion metric for airport of flight by getting the average delay at that airport for the hour of departure of the flight
df['airport_congestion'] = df.groupby(['ORIGIN_AIRPORT','hour'])['DEPARTURE_DELAY'].transform('mean')

# turnaround time (minutes)
df['turnaround_time'] = (df['dep_datetime'] - df['prev_arr_datetime']).dt.total_seconds() / 60

# invalid previous flight (arrival after departure)
invalid = df['prev_arr_datetime'] > df['dep_datetime']

# reset propagation features
df.loc[invalid, ['prev_arrival_delay']] = 0

# remove bad turnaround
df.loc[invalid, 'turnaround_time'] = np.nan

Insights and Reasoning¶

  • Sorted data set in chronological order by aircraft
  • Added columns to get the previous delay of the aircraft
  • created column to detail total turnaround time of the aircraft
  • created congestion matrix based on departure hour and how many flights from given airport were delayed in that hour with the larger congestion metric the more congested the airport was

#setting flights prev delay to 0 with turnaround time greater than 300
df.loc[df['turnaround_time'] > 300, ['prev_arrival_delay']] = 0

Isights and Reasoning¶

Setting previous delay as 0 for missing values with the assumption it is the first instance for that aircraft to therefore had no delay previously

Additionally decided to set previous delay to 0 for any flights with turnaround time greater than 300 as with that long between flights the previous flights delay should funtionally have no impact on the current flight

Correlation inbound vs outbound delay: 0.4690935566221489
P(outbound delay | inbound delay >15): 0.7044386676154228
P(outbound delay | No inbound delay >15): 0.10345803612020323

Insights:¶

When inbound flights are delayed outbound delay jumps from 10% to 70% showing a clear indication of delay propogation

Additionally the smaller correlation between the two could indicate that they have non-linear relationship

Overall Explanation and Takeaways from EDA and Data Prep¶

During this project we first decided to a few key preprocessing steps. These included handling missing values,and capping extreme delays to reduce distortion. One of the data prep steps that was challenging was ensuring accurate time-based calculations, as initial use of HHMM arithmetic produced incorrect turnaround values. This required converting to true datetime objects and carefully handling edge cases such as overnight flights. Another major challenge was correctly linking flights at the aircraft level. Using simple sorting and shifting initially led to mismatched “previous flights,” resulting in impossible negative turnaround times. This required additional validation logic to ensure that only valid prior flights were used, and to reset or filter cases where sequencing was incorrect. These issues highlighted how sensitive the analysis was to proper temporal alignment and data integrity.

After preprocessing we did Feature engineering. The focus here was on getting derived variables such as previous flight delays, turnaround time, time-of-day effects(hour variable) and a congestion metric based on average delay by airport and hour.

Finally after feature enineering we moved on to EDA which was able to show some important insights that will help with modeling. Most notably, delay propagation is a dominant factor: flights with a delayed inbound aircraft had about a 70% chance of departing late, compared to only about 10% otherwise. Turnaround time seem to exhibit a nonlinear relationship with delays, with moderate turnaround windows showing the highest delay risk, while long turnarounds allowed for recovery. Airline-level differences were substantial, with delay probabilities varying widely, indicating that operational strategies and network structures seem to play a major role. Additionally, airport congestion emerged as a key factor to consider in model building, while weather and security seem to show that they will not be as impactful in final analysis.
